arrival.speaker: narrator
arrival.text: Lin Yue reached the lower recruitment terrace with a worker's recommendation, forty-three copper coins and no sensed qi. Above her, Azure Cloud floated on an array she could not understand. She had spent seven years trying to cultivate after ordinary kiln shifts. The testing queue advanced one place. She tightened the cord around her bedding, loosened it again when her fingers cramped, and joined the other applicants.

pendant.speaker: lin_yue
pendant.text: At the upper gate, Yue held the jade in one hand and her release notes in the other. 'Three retained breath-units,' she told Qing before anyone asked. 'First stage. I can admit and discharge a trace. If that is too little for the work inside, tell me now.' The jade was warm, as it had been throughout every failed lesson. It had carried a memory. It had never carried her practice for her.

gate.speaker: shen_qing
gate.text: 'Your measured load is enough for a grounded relay, if we use one,' Qing said. 'It is not enough to feed the main array. You will remain behind its isolation line.' The gate bell sounded without a hand. Qing checked a gauge fixed to the post. Its needle had crossed the safe mark. He shut the qi-admission aperture before letting Yue through the gate's separate walking door.

introduction.speaker: lin_yue
introduction.text: 'I came because Elder Yun recognized the pendant,' Yue said. 'I still want to know why my mother gave it to me. I also want to know where this array releases its load. Every diagram I have copied has an exit stroke. I cannot find one on your gate.' Qing looked toward the tower. 'There is one,' he said. 'For nine centuries, nobody has expected to use it.'

first_choice.speaker: shen_qing
first_choice.text: Qing offered a padded testing cradle for the pendant. 'It may answer the sealed memory array. The cradle is grounded; your skin is not its fuel. We can test it before going farther, inspect the damaged gate gauge, or keep it wrapped until Yun explains the lake.' Yue looked at the unfamiliar circuit and the release stroke she knew. She would have to choose what she could verify first.

choices.text: Test the jade in the grounded cradle.
Read the gate's damaged pressure gauge.
Keep the jade wrapped until its circuit is explained.

trust.speaker: shen_qing
trust.text: Yue placed the jade in the cradle. Qing let her direct the small release trace she had practiced for weeks, then supplied the array's required fuel from a separate stone. The jade stopped trembling. 'Good closure,' Qing said. 'The memory response came from the object. The controlled trace came from you. Keep both measurements separate.' Yue retrieved the pendant before they left the gate.

question.speaker: shen_qing
question.text: The gauge recorded rising pressure from the mountain's lifting array. 'Our founder bound a living star below the reservoir,' Qing said. 'The array has drawn from it for nine hundred years. Three nights ago the return circuit stopped balancing the intake.' Yue read the rated load on the plate. Her own reserve would not move its smallest main valve. Finding the release path would matter more.

guard.speaker: shen_qing
guard.text: Yue kept the pendant wrapped. 'I will not connect it to a circuit whose closure I do not understand.' Qing nodded and opened the ordinary stair gate instead. 'Then we use the gauges until Yun explains the cradle. Keep your qi inside the load you have tested. Strange light in this corridor belongs to the field; it is not evidence that your realm has changed.'

courtyard.speaker: narrator
courtyard.text: Plum petals rose through the courtyard because the lifting field was leaking into the air above the isolation rails. Yue remembered the practice wick that had lit too easily on the lower stair. She kept admission closed. A faint voice came from beneath the pavilion, where the main array met the buried reservoir. She could hear it with her ears. She did not have to send a trace toward it.

elder.speaker: elder_yun
elder.text: Yun stood beside a shut fuel cabinet. 'Your mother's eyes,' she said, then looked at her notebook. 'And work she never had the chance to record.' Yue wanted that recognition to explain her faint root. Yun did not offer the explanation. 'Your examination was yours. This pendant concerns a different debt. I owe you its account before asking for help.'

mother.speaker: lin_yue
mother.text: 'You knew the jade was here,' Yue said. 'You watched me fail tests without mentioning her. Why?' Yun took the question before the cabinet keys. 'Because her history was not a safe substitute for your training. I also delayed because the history shames me.' Yue kept the wrapped pendant in her palm. 'Then tell it before we make another circuit.'

truth.speaker: elder_yun
truth.text: 'The jade holds an offered memory of an afternoon beside the star,' Yun said. 'Your mother brought kindness where the founder's array had left only demand. It is a memory vessel, not a root, core or cultivation inheritance. Opening its projection will not consume its casing. Connecting that memory may let the star recognize why we came. It cannot give you the capacity to carry a mountain.'

cultivation_choice.speaker: elder_yun
cultivation_choice.text: Yun spread three preparation sheets on the pavilion table. The crisis had no room for a new realm. Yue could calibrate her small relay, compare the release inscription with the founder's plan, or rehearse the marked evacuation path. Each used skills she already possessed. Their preparation circuits would remain isolated from the live main array while they worked.

choices.text: Calibrate the small relay at your safe load.
Compare the release inscription with the old plan.
Rehearse the marked evacuation path.

breath.speaker: narrator
breath.text: Yue used the grounded practice wick from her examination. She admitted a trace, closed it and measured the release three times. Qing adjusted a relay so its input would trip below Yue's safe load. The preparation improved her familiarity with this circuit. Her lower dantian remained the same small reservoir she had brought up the stairs. She had earned a safer task, not another stage.

inscription.speaker: lin_yue
inscription.text: Yue compared the founder's drawing to the array plate. The exit stroke ended short of its grounding mark, exactly where her first ordinary ink copies had failed. 'The shelter circuit was altered to hold its source,' she said. Yun checked her reading against the older rubbing. Her useful discovery came from a month of dull pages that had never once shone.

sword.speaker: lin_yue
sword.text: Yue walked the evacuation path with her ordinary blade sheathed. She checked the rail, the turn where two people could not pass and the signal for stopping the descent. Sword drills had taught her to move without crossing her feet. Today that skill would help someone follow her in darkness. The blade would not cut an ancient main seal. She marked the safe turn with white chalk.

exile.speaker: mo_ran
exile.text: Yun brought the older rubbing to the preparation table. On it the exit reached its grounding mark; on the installed plate it ended short. She showed the discrepancy to Qing and Yue before they approached the reservoir. Mo Ran entered by the maintenance stair with grounding cable. A pale crack showed along his wrist. Yun identified a return injury from an old core circuit. His useful account and their shared comparison still needed checking against the pressure gauges.

accusation.speaker: shen_qing
accusation.text: 'Your sentence forbids this stair,' Qing said. 'The outer pressure seal was disturbed this morning.' Mo Ran kept his hands away from the console. 'After the reservoir reflux. Check the gauge times; if they contradict me, I will wait outside.' Qing checked the sequence. The field disturbance came first, without settling responsibility for every seal. Yun signed a temporary emergency-maintenance pass within Mo Ran's injury limit. Qing admitted him under that pass. The original sentence and unresolved accusation remained recorded.

exile_truth.speaker: mo_ran
exile_truth.text: 'I listened through the speaking conduit,' Mo Ran said. 'No soul projection and no broken seal. The star asked whether anyone would stop drawing from it.' Yue looked at the ancient reservoir plan. Its source was drawn as a circle with no exit of its own. Even a novice could see that the drawing treated a living being like a stone that would never run out.

listen_choice.speaker: lin_yue
listen_choice.text: Before they entered the reservoir stair, Yue asked for one account that could change the plan. The star's wish, the people exposed above, and Yun's earlier failure each had consequences for closing the array. Her notebook held room for facts. It did not hold enough reserve to solve a question she chose to ignore.

choices.text: Ask the exile what the star wants.
Ask Shen Qing who he is protecting.
Ask Elder Yun why she waited.

star_wants.speaker: mo_ran
star_wants.text: 'It wants rest and a way to leave,' Mo Ran said. 'I asked through the conduit, then repeated the answer so it could correct me. It did. It does not want the village crushed as the price of leaving.' He pointed to the dormant support anchors on the plan. 'We may have an exit for everyone, if we stop treating the current arrangement as the only possible one.'

protection.speaker: shen_qing
protection.text: 'Three hundred disciples and the village under the field,' Qing said. 'Most disciples are Body Tempering or early Qi Gathering. Counting names does not give us three hundred equal fuel sources. We need rated relays, independent stones, rest rotations and a closure if anyone withdraws. I have been guarding this gate for eleven years. I should have practiced the exit before tonight.'

waiting.speaker: elder_yun
waiting.text: 'Your mother reached the lake and helped the star survive another season,' Yun said. 'I accepted that postponement as if it were a repair. Her technique cost years of recovery she never regained. She brought back the jade and told me to change the seal. I kept the mountain running. Fear can look like duty while somebody else pays its cultivation cost.'

descent.speaker: narrator
descent.text: The reservoir stair descended beside an intact grounding rail. Qing checked each landing before Yue followed. Below, a lake without reflection covered the source chamber. The star was small enough to shelter in two hands, yet the array surrounding it covered the cavern roof. Yue stopped behind the isolation line. She could feel pressure there without admitting it. Her first useful discipline was keeping her own circuit shut.

star.speaker: narrator
star.text: A voice came through the speaking conduit above the lake. 'Did she send you? The woman who sat beside me while I forgot the names of my constellations?' Yue could answer in ordinary speech. Yun checked the return gauge while Qing kept the stair open. Nothing required the novice to surrender her mind, touch the source water or pretend to understand the star's inner cultivation.

answer.speaker: lin_yue
answer.text: 'She gave me a memory to carry here,' Yue said. 'I could not travel safely then. I have learned enough to reach you now, and enough to know I cannot promise what I cannot sustain.' She asked whether the star wanted the memory projected. After the answer, Yun set the grounded cradle beside the conduit. Yue kept hold of the pendant until its release path was checked.

memory.speaker: narrator
memory.text: The projection showed her mother sharing an orange beside the lake. The casing remained whole in the cradle. The memory's brief light drew from its stored image charge, not from Yue's root or the star's unoffered thoughts. She watched without acquiring her technique. When the projection ended, she lifted the warm jade again. The useful inheritance was the example of someone sitting down to listen.

fracture.speaker: shen_qing
fracture.text: The return gauge climbed. Qing isolated the star's intake while Yun transferred the lifting load to stored support anchors. Their checked fuel covered this transition, not endless suspension. The gauge confirmed that no new draw crossed the source line before anyone opened its escape gate. Mo Ran inspected the grounding cable within his injury limit. Yue stayed behind the relay's trip. They could discuss a lower voluntary draw, an interval outside or a controlled landing while the temporary anchors carried the immediate load.

final_choice.speaker: lin_yue
final_choice.text: Yue laid the corrected release diagram beside the fuel account. They could distribute temporary support through rated relays, build a covenant with a usable exit, or ground the mountain through its old landing anchors. If her preparation was insufficient, the others could coordinate the established emergency procedure. None would turn her first qi trace into a higher realm.

choices.text: Coordinate support through rated willing relays.
Help repair the covenant's missing release.
Signal the mountain's controlled landing.
Call the trained emergency teams together.

shared.speaker: lin_yue
shared.text: 'Use my relay only within its tested load,' Yue said. Qing connected the separately fueled support branches; she supplied one small closure pulse. Yun restored only the lower source draw the star had confirmed, with its manual escape and stop signal available. Yue stopped at the relay's scheduled limit. Each willing operator had a rated turn and a replacement. Before dusk, the sect would review the auxiliary fuel instead of calling three hundred volunteers an inexhaustible supply.

covenant.speaker: lin_yue
covenant.text: Yue showed where the missing release stroke met the grounding mark. Yun inscribed it with established core control; Qing tested the exit. Engineers measured additional sect-reserve charge for the star's interval outside until sunset, retaining enough for a controlled landing. Operators accepted those bounded turns. If the star declined return, landing would begin before the reserve floor. The covenant preserved the star's departure choice. Yue's understanding let her assist; the carving power and support fuel came from elsewhere.

release.speaker: lin_yue
release.text: Yue followed the marked evacuation route to the landing console. Qing and Yun sequenced the earthward anchors while Mo Ran kept the return load below his injury limit. The ordinary sword stayed sheathed. Yue carried a signal between sheltered stations and watched the descent by measured stages. The already isolated source intake stayed closed. Only after the supports secured the mountain on earth did Yun retire the temporary lifting anchors. The star departed through the open conduit without bearing the landing load.

together.speaker: shen_qing
together.text: Qing called the established emergency teams. Yue read the corrected release sheet aloud while Yun opened the separately fueled support branches. Operators accepted or declined rated turns and kept the grounding path available. After the branches stabilized, Yun restored only the star's confirmed lower draw, retaining its stop signal and manual escape. Yue remained outside the main load. Asking for help had not advanced her realm. It had kept her limited capacity inside a workable plan.

ending_shared.speaker: narrator
ending_shared.text: At dawn, temporary support lanterns marked the mountain paths. Independent stones fed the rated branches while willing operators took short control turns. The star carried a smaller agreed load and could request another rest. Azure Cloud remained aloft with a fuel deadline it now had to honor. Yue returned to the lower terrace at Qi Gathering's first stage. The work tablet still hung beneath her examination cord.

ending_covenant.speaker: narrator
ending_covenant.text: The star rose through the open source conduit, then chose to return at sunset under the new bounded covenant. Azure Cloud remained aloft while stored anchors carried the interval. Yun planted an orange tree beside the lake after arranging the next fuel review. Yue kept the intact pendant and copied the corrected exit into her notebook. Her own next task was still a recovered morning measurement.

ending_release.speaker: narrator
ending_release.text: The landing anchors took the mountain's weight in measured stages, leaving every roof below intact. The star departed into the open sky. Azure Cloud stood on earth, and the old exile boundary no longer enclosed Mo Ran's road. Yue rested the intact jade against the ground, then lifted it again. She had helped with a transition using a novice's bounded task. Tomorrow she would practice the same first-stage circuit.

lantern_shared.speaker: narrator
lantern_shared.text: Azure Cloud remained aloft under the star's bounded lower load. At the first morning fuel review, the sect funded the auxiliary branches from its maintenance account for seven days and posted the next review before expiry. The escape gate stayed usable. Later renewals would need fresh fuel and accepted operator turns; a request to stop required switching to rated supports or landing. Lin Yue kept her first-stage field. While engineers repaired the valley road, Shen Qing offered her paid sluice work.

lantern_covenant.speaker: narrator
lantern_covenant.text: The star accepted its covenant. The displaced valley paths still need engineers, meals and patient repairs. Elder Yun gives Lin Yue a future place on the listening commission, with no promotion attached. For now she can earn wages at the brine sluice and practice under its examiner. Her mother's offered memory supplies neither fuel nor a finished meridian.

lantern_release.speaker: narrator
lantern_release.text: The released mountain has roots, and the drainage channels beneath it need rebuilding before the valley road opens. Mo Ran asks Lin Yue to join the later survey. Today she remains a first-stage novice whose field leaks during sleep. He directs her to a paid sluice placement, where useful work and slow cultivation can share the waiting weeks.

lantern_arrival.speaker: narrator
lantern_arrival.text: The road ended at a lake black enough to hold every lantern twice. Lin Yue tested her travel thread in shade before approaching the bell tower. Salt wind changed its blank by a small interval; she wrote the correction instead of claiming another breakthrough. Her field held third-stage charge. The village's enormous boundary ward drew power from buried stones, while every gate bore a strip of blank paper.

lantern_clapper.speaker: su_lan
lantern_clapper.text: Do not write your name on those slips. They are not invitations. Last winter the lake took nineteen names from our register, and the magistrate decided that people with no names could not own land. We leave the paper empty so visitors will ask before lending us another pretty solution.

lantern_introduction.speaker: lin_yue
lantern_introduction.text: I am Lin Yue, third-stage Qi Gathering under Azure Cloud's first-pair method. I brought a calibrated thread, a grounding tail and a limited reserve. None returns a household name. If there is a rated relay I may test it under supervision; if there is ordinary work, I can take my share. First I need to hear what the boundary actually does.

lantern_empty_bell.speaker: su_lan
lantern_empty_bell.text: Su Lan. Keeper is a job that pays in complaints. The bell has no clapper because I took it down. Each time it sounded, another household vanished from the register. People said the beast in the reeds was eating our names. People also said the magistrate was saving us. Both stories were very convenient.

lantern_map.speaker: narrator
lantern_map.text: Su Lan spread a salt-stained map beside the nineteen household names. Wei Xiu's north landing lay across a ferry route. The marsh trail reached a roofless shrine; the archive had been crossed out and drawn again. Copper marks identified the ward's buried fuel stations. Lin Yue recognized a distribution circuit too large for her field and asked who inspected it. Su Lan wrote those workers beside the map's existing witnesses.

lantern_hub.speaker: su_lan
lantern_hub.text: We have until tomorrow evening's tide before the magistrate seals the register. Wei Jin's ferry can reach the drowned boundary stones. The Reed Listener is nesting at the roofless shrine. An Ru is hiding the old ledger in the archive. Choose where we should help. I have asked the other witnesses to bring their findings to the tower; one person cannot visit every road.

choices.text: Follow the ferry and find who moved the boundary.
Enter the marsh and listen to the accused spirit.
Visit the archive and trace the missing names.

ferry_departure.speaker: narrator
ferry_departure.text: Wei Jin's ferry was held together by rope, lacquer, and the stubbornness of a man who could mend everything except an official letter. He kept a pot of ginger tea beneath the tiller. On the landing, a carved stone named the lake a public crossing. A fresh seal declared every crossing a trespass.

ferry_price.speaker: wei_jin
ferry_price.text: You can pay me when you return. That makes you passengers rather than witnesses, according to the clerk who wrote this notice. I have carried the same families for thirty years. If I call them customers now, perhaps their homes will become real enough for the magistrate to tax them.

ferry_mark.speaker: su_lan
ferry_mark.text: His daughter carved the crossing stone. Her household was one of the nineteen. Her name is Wei Xiu; she is alive, working at the north landing. Saying it does not restore her deed, but I say it whenever I pass. Be careful with the word missing. Sometimes it describes a person; sometimes it describes what somebody has chosen to stop seeing.

ferry_water.speaker: narrator
ferry_water.text: Terraces slid beneath the hull like pale stairs into an unlit house. Lin Yue kept the pendant closed against her robe and lowered an unpowered sighting mirror beside the drowned boundary stone. Wei Jin steadied it with a rope. Two inscriptions came into view: an older face toward the village and a newer clause turned inward beneath the water. Her first pair supplied no sight through stone; the ordinary mirror supplied the angle.

ferry_discovery.speaker: lin_yue
ferry_discovery.text: Someone turned the boundary inward. The village side says common water. The submerged side says private refuge. Last winter, the revised register let the ward enforce that hidden inscription against the nineteen households. It did not steal the fields by accident. It obeyed an old instruction once the new ink classified the owners as strangers.

ferry_warning.speaker: wei_jin
ferry_warning.text: A lever and two ferry capstans can raise the stone without rotating it. My crews know the lifting load. Su Lan knows the ward's isolation latch. Your qi can test its small relay through a rated adapter, if your blank stays stable. The stone's shelter runs on buried fuel, not your body. Turning it too quickly could expose the winter pans even if every rope holds.

ferry_choice.speaker: su_lan
ferry_choice.text: We can raise the stone with the ward intact, share its shelter with the banks, or leave it until the villagers can move the pans. Every answer costs someone a night of work. Before you choose, tell us whose work you think you have the right to volunteer.

choices.text: Raise the stone publicly, keeping its protective ward intact.
Ask the boat crews to share the ward, one willing crew at a time.
Mark the boundary and let the village vote after seeing it.

ferry_raise.speaker: lin_yue
ferry_raise.text: Let the crews lift the stone while Su Lan holds the isolation latch. I can send one quarter-unit through its rated status relay after checking the blank, then discharge. I will not take the lifting load through an unfinished route. Once both faces are visible, everyone can read them while the separately fueled shelter remains. That gives the village evidence before any decision to rotate the boundary.

ferry_raise_cost.speaker: narrator
ferry_raise_cost.text: Capstans creaked and the hidden inscription broke the surface. Lin Yue's small pulse crossed the adapter; its reference showed the ward still drawing from the buried stones. She discharged before the crews changed the rope load. Salt caught an existing crack in her glove and stung her palm. She replaced the glove and stopped testing. Across the lake, workers copied both exposed clauses while Su Lan maintained the latch.

ferry_share.speaker: wei_jin
ferry_share.text: I will ask the west-bank crews. You ask the east. Do not say that good people must agree, and do not let the magistrate stand beside you while you ask. A yes given in front of a seal can be another kind of no. Bring me the refusals as carefully as the promises.

ferry_share_cost.speaker: narrator
ferry_share_cost.text: Five crews offered oil, two ropes, and three refused because winter had emptied their stores. Su Lan recorded each answer and mapped the gaps before changing any ward link. The crews fueled a temporary shelter with separately inspected stones; the unconnected shore remained protected by the existing arrangement. Lin Yue tested one low-load relay, then stopped. Her finite field could measure an allowed connection; it could not cover the missing shore.

ferry_wait.speaker: su_lan
ferry_wait.text: Then our work tonight is evidence. We will mark where the common water ended and where the private refuge began. The villagers will decide what to move. Waiting can be cowardice, Yue, but sometimes it is the courage to let another person arrive at an answer you cannot predict.

ferry_wait_cost.speaker: narrator
ferry_wait_cost.text: They anchored three lanterns around the stone and drew its position on the map. The ferryman returned without reclaiming a single pan. At the landing, a worker called them useless. Su Lan handed her the map and listened until the anger had a shape. By midnight, the workers had planned a crossing of their own.

ferry_evidence.speaker: wei_jin
ferry_evidence.text: Take this comparison copy to the tower. The crews transcribed both faces through our ordinary sighting mirror before we chose whether to lift the stone. The magistrate's grandfather signed the private refuge clause. My grandmother signed the common-water line. We have inherited both. I cannot make either ancestor answer for it. I can stand beside you when someone asks what I intend to do with my inheritance.

ferry_return.speaker: narrator
ferry_return.text: At the village landing, the ferry sat without triumphant music, its leak an inch longer. Su Lan paid the agreed passenger fare from her travel purse. Wei Jin then charged for three cups of tea; she bought four and left one steaming by the crossing stone. Lin Yue carried the comparison beneath her robe, where the pendant could not mistake a document for a destiny.

reed_approach.speaker: narrator
reed_approach.text: The marsh path narrowed between translucent reeds. Every blade held a thread of cold light. Lin Yue heard a bell, then noticed that the sound stopped whenever she tried to follow it. Su Lan removed her bronze clapper from its cord and laid it on the path. The reeds leaned away, leaving room for two people to pass.

reed_old_wound.speaker: su_lan
reed_old_wound.text: I struck the bell last winter, when my husband's name disappeared from our household record. He had been dead for six winters already. The magistrate said the bell would restore his place in the register. It called the ward instead. For months I blamed the beast because that story left me someone to hate. Remember that when I sound certain.

reed_nest.speaker: narrator
reed_nest.text: At the roofless shrine stood a creature with wet-slate feathers and salt reeds along its spine. A bronze bell hung at its throat. Paper nests held unmarked household tablets. Lin Yue's copper reference case clicked against her belt, and the Listener shielded the nests. She closed the case at once. A measuring instrument, like a blade, could be a threat when brought into another being's shelter without asking.

reed_voice.speaker: reed_listener
reed_voice.text: A measuring case can be a demand even when its copper is quiet. Keep yours closed, away from the nests, until I agree to a particular test. I cannot know its purpose from your intentions. Tell me which household you came to ask about, and whether its people have agreed to a return. My shelter is no invitation to read a tablet merely because you have learned to guide a trace.

reed_question.speaker: lin_yue
reed_question.text: Wei Xiu. And eighteen others whose names I have not earned the right to speak yet. I thought you might have stolen them. These nests look like shelter. What are you protecting them from, Listener? And what happens if the people outside never learn where their names have gone?

reed_answer.speaker: reed_listener
reed_answer.text: The bell commands the boundary to keep what it recognizes. The register recognizes a household by its name. When the new ink called those households trespassers, I took the names where the bell could not find them. Their people remained alive. Their doors became empty to the ward. Protection is a crooked nest when the wind comes from every side.

reed_hunger.speaker: narrator
reed_hunger.text: One nest trembled. A child's handwriting appeared on its tablet, then faded. The Listener lowered its head. Every name it sheltered cost a memory of its own. It no longer remembered whether it had once been a crane, a reed, or the first sound a ferryman heard on the lake. Its refuge would not survive another winter.

reed_choice.speaker: lin_yue
reed_choice.text: I can carry the tablets to the tower, help you change the bell's command, or defend the shrine while the villagers come here themselves. I will not call any of these gifts unless you can refuse it. You have been protecting people who did not know how to thank you. That should not become another sentence.

choices.text: Escort the tablets under the Listener's protection.
Study the bell's command together and change its boundary.
Bring the families here so each can reclaim their own name.

reed_escort.speaker: reed_listener
reed_escort.text: Carry the nests, not loose tablets. A name is lighter than paper and heavier than a promise. If a clerk demands that you open one before its owner arrives, say no. If that no puts a sword between you and the tower, ask me before you decide whose blood should pay for it.

reed_escort_cost.speaker: narrator
reed_escort_cost.text: They carried the paper nests on a reed litter. At the shrine gate, a patrol demanded proof that the tablets belonged to living households. Lin Yue set her sword on the earth and asked the patrol captain to bring those households instead. The captain hesitated long enough for Su Lan to recognize him as a boy she had taught to read.

reed_rewrite.speaker: lin_yue
reed_rewrite.text: The command links a recognized name to an enforced boundary. I can trace its low-power test copy; I cannot carry the lake's ward load or carve a new spiritual law into this bell. Will you describe the rhythm before a name disappears? Su Lan can isolate the test circuit, and we can search for an interruption that leaves a household time to answer.

reed_rewrite_cost.speaker: narrator
reed_rewrite_cost.text: The Listener tapped a rhythm on an unpowered shrine tile. Su Lan copied it into a blank test strip, safely separated from the nests. The first simulation rejected its dummy name; the second overfilled its small fuel channel. Lin Yue grounded the strip and stopped. At the third, Su Lan left a pause for the spoken reply. The simulation accepted it without drawing more than its allotted stone charge. No real tablet had been risked.

reed_families.speaker: su_lan
reed_families.text: I will fetch them. Some will be frightened of you, Listener. Some will be angry. You may be angry in return. I cannot promise a meeting without hurt. I can promise that the first person who calls you a monster will hear from the keeper who taught the village that word.

reed_families_cost.speaker: narrator
reed_families_cost.text: The families arrived with lanterns, food, and two farm hooks carried as weapons. A child asked whether the Listener ate fish. An old man asked why it had not explained itself sooner. The creature could answer only one question at a time. Lin Yue stayed beside the sheltered nests until dawn, learning how long a safe meeting could take.

reed_memory.speaker: reed_listener
reed_memory.text: One of the names has returned something to me. Before I was this body, I listened beneath a bridge. Boats passed above me, and no one asked the water to be grateful. Keep that memory if I lose it again. I would like to know that I belonged here before anyone needed saving.

reed_return.speaker: narrator
reed_return.text: Su Lan tied the clapper to her wrist again. She had not rung it, but the cord no longer looked like a punishment. The Listener followed them toward the tower at the pace of a creature carrying a village's winter in its feathers. Along the path, the reeds began to sound like reeds instead of warnings.

archive_door.speaker: narrator
archive_door.text: The archive door had been sealed with wet ink. An Ru opened it from inside using a kettle, a knife, and a patience Lin Yue immediately envied. Shelves leaned under rolls of household records. On the reading table lay nineteen cards, each bearing a name. At first glance nothing was missing. Then Lin Yue noticed the dates.

archive_copies.speaker: an_ru
archive_copies.text: These are copies made yesterday. The missing families appear as newcomers requesting permission to settle land their grandparents farmed. The magistrate offered to restore their names if they signed. He called it mercy. I kept the originals because mercy should survive comparison with the document it replaces.

archive_ancestry.speaker: su_lan
archive_ancestry.text: My husband is on that card. It says he arrived this spring. He died seven winters ago, standing in the water to rescue a ferry rope. The clerk copied his name from my complaint without copying the reason I had written it. So there he is, applying for a home he had already left feet first.

archive_dilemma.speaker: an_ru
archive_dilemma.text: The originals prove the village's claim, but they also record debts. Wei Jin's family owes the shrine seventeen years of maintenance. The keeper's house borrowed seed salt during the famine. If we publish everything, the magistrate will demand payment. If we hide the debts, he will call the entire archive forged.

archive_reading.speaker: narrator
archive_reading.text: Lin Yue read the land conditions beside maintenance entries for the ward's fuel stations. Debts had witnesses, dates and exceptions: salt only after a harvest surplus, shared maintenance when the ferry carried shrine visitors. The new copies kept the numbers and removed the conditions. She recognized the same distortion as an examination that reported reserve but hid sampling loss. Here it could erase a household's claim, not merely flatter a novice's result.

archive_question.speaker: lin_yue
archive_question.text: He has made generosity look like a failed bargain. We can expose the full ledger, restore the exceptions first, or ask each household what it permits us to reveal. There is no clean page waiting behind these pages. There are only people who have to live together after we put the book down.

archive_choice.speaker: an_ru
archive_choice.text: Choose how we bring this to the tower. I can preserve the pages whichever way you go. I cannot preserve everyone's trust by deciding what they ought to feel about them. Before you ask a clerk to be brave, remember that tomorrow the clerk still needs to work in this room.

choices.text: Publish the original land clauses and every condition, preserving private debts.
Build a comparison showing exactly which exceptions were removed.
Ask the households to choose what may be read in public.

archive_publish.speaker: lin_yue
archive_publish.text: We will take the whole ledger so the originals can be checked. Public copies will include the land clauses and every condition beside them; personal debts need their households' permission before a reading. I will stay through the hearing. If anyone uses a debt to erase a household's right to speak, I will ask them to read its exception out loud.

archive_publish_cost.speaker: narrator
archive_publish_cost.text: An Ru wrapped the ledger in oilcloth. Su Lan stopped at a page bearing her husband's mark and stood very still. It recorded a loan she had never known he made. The discovery did not diminish the years they had shared, but it changed their edges. Truth had arrived as grief before it could become evidence.

archive_compare.speaker: an_ru
archive_compare.text: Then we need two columns, not an accusation. Here is what the village agreed. Here is what the copy claims. I will put my own name beneath the comparison. People should be able to question the person who assembled their proof, even if that questioning makes the proof harder to use.

archive_compare_cost.speaker: narrator
archive_compare_cost.text: They copied until the kettle went cold. Twice Lin Yue read a clause too quickly; twice An Ru made her start again. One exception favored the magistrate's own house, whose winter roof had been rebuilt without charge. Su Lan insisted they preserve that line too. A fair ledger could not begin by finding a new household to erase.

archive_consent.speaker: su_lan
archive_consent.text: We will knock on doors before we open this book in the square. A household can refuse us, and we will record the refusal without inventing a reason. We will explain that silence may weaken the case. Then we will leave the door open long enough for the answer to belong to them.

archive_consent_cost.speaker: narrator
archive_consent_cost.text: Seven households permitted every page. Six permitted the land records but kept their debts private. Four asked An Ru to read for them. Two refused. Lin Yue wanted to argue with the last two until Su Lan pointed out how closely her helpful speech resembled the magistrate's offer of mercy.

archive_witness.speaker: an_ru
archive_witness.text: Take my seal, Yue. It proves that these extracts came from this room. It does not prove that you must agree with me. If the magistrate asks who authorized a private reading, show the permission recorded for that page. A household's name on a door is no permission; a refusal remains a refusal. Public land clauses can be checked separately. If he asks who authorized my work, say that I did, and bring him here.

archive_return.speaker: narrator
archive_return.text: They left the archive with paper heavier than any sword. An Ru remained behind to make copies for the households who had asked. The blank slips at the gates began to fill: a name, a question, a date, a refusal. The village did not speak with one voice. Lin Yue began to think that might be the first good sign.

lantern_conclave.speaker: narrator
lantern_conclave.text: At the tower, Su Lan isolated the bell's enforcement link while crews checked the existing shelter's stones. Lanterns gathered in uneven rings. The magistrate arrived with a clean register and an offer to simplify the claims. Lin Yue kept her field closed; this hearing needed witnesses before power. She had enough evidence to expose the omissions and enough cultivation experience to distrust a clean number with its operating conditions removed.

lantern_magistrate.speaker: su_lan
lantern_magistrate.text: You may speak first, Yue. But before you speak for this village, look at it. There are people who agreed with you, people who refused you, and people whose problem you did not have time to visit. A beautiful answer can still leave someone standing outside its light.

lantern_final_choice.speaker: lin_yue
lantern_final_choice.text: The magistrate could not reconcile the new dates with the witnessed originals. He countersigned corrections restoring all nineteen household entries; the clerk gave each household its copy. Separate boundary disputes remained open. With enforcement still isolated, the owners could decide their tablets' return. Now we can make a common crossing, change the bell's answering rule, rebuild the shrine's shelter, or begin a public ledger anyone may question. None will mend every wound tonight. Which work are we ready to remain for after the lanterns go out?

choices.text: Open the crossing and share responsibility for its ward.
Teach the bell to wait for an answer before enforcing a boundary.
Plant a living shelter where the old refuge took root.
Begin a public ledger and return the decisions to the village.

lantern_crossing.speaker: wei_jin
lantern_crossing.text: I will sail the first crossing at dawn. After that, the crews will choose their own turns. The people who refused the ward still have the right to use the landing. If we start charging agreement as a fare, we have learned nothing from the stone under the water.

ending_crossing.speaker: narrator
ending_crossing.text: The hearing restored the nineteen household records before the first public crossing. Each lantern had an owner; each owner could take it home. The ward held because enough people returned the next evening, then the next. Lin Yue stayed to mend ropes. The mountain's promise had reached the valley as work that could be shared and refused.

lantern_bell.speaker: reed_listener
lantern_bell.text: Su Lan has agreed to lend her clapper under her supervision until sunset. I will strike once for every restored name and wait until someone answers. If no one answers, I will wait longer. A boundary that cannot bear a pause has no right to tell a living person where to stand.

ending_bell.speaker: narrator
ending_bell.text: The ward crew installed the answering rule with enforcement isolated. Using its existing stone supply and dummy records, they verified answered boundaries and unanswered holds before enabling the revised link. The nineteen restored entries remained intact. The twentieth note belonged to the Listener, whose own name no one yet knew. Su Lan left a blank line for it. This time the blank was room to arrive. She reclaimed her clapper at sunset. Lin Yue listened beside the tower until the reeds answered in the evening wind.

lantern_seed.speaker: lin_yue
lantern_seed.text: The hearing returns the names while the clapper remains isolated. For future shelter, I can test one nursery relay through a rated pot; its stone supplies the charge and ordinary hands supply water. My first pair guides a bounded pulse. It cannot make salt harmless or force roots to grow. Nobody's claim will wait for a leaf, and the carpenter's roof work continues whichever seed succeeds.

ending_seed.speaker: narrator
ending_seed.text: The hearing restored all nineteen records. The first seed failed in brackish soil; the second survived after a measured clean-water wash and a different pot. Lin Yue kept the failed readings beside the surviving nursery relay's fuel account. Through winter, villagers shared the ordinary warmth and tending. In spring she found three leaves, still no fourth-stage claim, and a roof repaired by paid carpenters. The future grove remained a small living experiment.

lantern_ledger.speaker: an_ru
lantern_ledger.text: We will begin with the changes, the disagreements, and the names of the people who made them. A ledger is useful only if another hand can correct it. I will keep the first copy. The second belongs in the square. The third should travel with someone willing to return when it is challenged.

ending_ledger.speaker: narrator
ending_ledger.text: Lin Yue left Salt Lantern Valley with a book instead of a verdict. Behind her, nineteen households read their names in their own hands. Ahead, other villages had blank paper on their gates. She could not promise each one an ending. She could promise to arrive with questions, and to leave room on the page for an answer.

assembly_ferry.speaker: wei_jin
assembly_ferry.text: I went to the boundary, with the west-bank crews if you were elsewhere. This comparison records both faces of the stone. My grandmother signed the common-water line. The magistrate's grandfather signed the private refuge clause. Neither signature gives a living person permission to erase another. I have brought the crews so you can question our account.

assembly_archive.speaker: an_ru
assembly_archive.text: I brought a comparison of the land clauses. The personal debts remain covered unless their households have permitted a reading. Here are the dates and the exceptions missing from the new copies. You may check them against the originals in my room. A copied accusation deserves the same scrutiny as a copied defense.

assembly_listener.speaker: reed_listener
assembly_listener.text: The families brought these nests, and I followed. The keeper's message asked us to come to the tower; it did not command us to surrender the tablets. Each nest holds a household's name beyond the bell's recognition. No person was swallowed. When the ward can hear them safely, their owners will decide how the tablets return.

assembly_test.speaker: narrator
assembly_test.text: An Ru placed a disputed copy beside the crossing comparison. Su Lan held the clapper still and kept the enforcement circuit isolated. A salt worker named her household; the old register recognized it, the new copy did not. The Listener uncovered the matching nest without surrendering it. Lin Yue observed the same omission in three records. No pulse through her first pair could replace that comparison, and no bright instrument could authorize a private reading.

assembly_magistrate.speaker: an_ru
assembly_magistrate.text: The magistrate says a single register prevents conflicting claims. That is true. He also says only his copies can settle a conflict. That is the part we dispute. He may answer each discrepancy here, with the witnesses present. No one is being asked to exchange a land claim for agreement with our proposed repairs.

assembly_provisional.speaker: su_lan
assembly_provisional.text: The original dates can be checked, and sealing is suspended until this hearing ends. I have isolated the bell's enforcement link. The crews inspect the existing shelter's fuel every watch; disputed households may enter without signing new claims. That buys a measured interval of safety. It does not settle ownership. Each household still gets an answer before we reconnect any revised command to the boundary.

assembly_shelter.speaker: wei_jin
assembly_shelter.text: The shrine's old orange grove died when salt reached the roots. I saved two seeds. No name will remain in the Listener's care merely to power a seed experiment. The carpenter can repair a roof separately, and our fuel workers can shelter that work. If you propose a growing ward, state its water, soil and stone costs. A right to a home cannot depend on whether a novice's first tree survives.

river_from_crossing.speaker: wei_jin
river_from_crossing.text: Through winter, the crews kept a rota beside the repaired crossing. Some withdrew; others joined. Nobody lost passage for taking a lantern home. By spring, Lin Yue had learned three ways to splice a rope and one way to recognize a duty she had begun enjoying. Then Wei Xiu came from the north landing with a chart showing a ferry that had returned to the same bend twelve times.

river_from_bell.speaker: su_lan
river_from_bell.text: Through winter, the bell waited for answers before the ward changed a boundary. It did not become wiser than the people listening; twice we corrected it together. The Listener's blank line remains blank by its choice. In spring, my husband would have been dead eight winters. I carried flowers to the crossing, and Wei Xiu brought news of a ferry that could not finish its journey.

river_from_seed.speaker: narrator
river_from_seed.text: In the spring promised by three small leaves, Lin Yue returned to Su Lan's door. The pot was warm, and the shrine's paid roof repair was complete. The carpenter inspected its joints after winter rather than measuring an unfinished roof again. Wei Xiu arrived with a river chart showing a ferry circling one bend without passengers. A surviving seed and a repaired shelter had not settled this different obligation. Lin Yue packed her third-stage reference thread before following the pilot.

river_from_ledger.speaker: an_ru
river_from_ledger.text: Lin Yue traveled during autumn, then returned after winter with corrections from three villages. I entered those beside our own, leaving the old versions visible. The nineteen households had kept their restored records. The magistrate still disputed two boundaries, which the hearing had not settled. On the morning we reopened those questions, Wei Xiu reported another kind of unfinished crossing.

river_arrival.speaker: narrator
river_arrival.text: At the north landing, rain flattened the river into a sheet of hammered pewter. Wei Xiu stood beside the stone she had carved, rubbing chalk into its shallow letters. The record at the archive now recognized her household. The stone needed no new name. Lin Yue found comfort in work whose purpose was visible: clean a groove, mend a rope, leave the person standing where she had always stood.

river_xiu.speaker: wei_xiu
river_xiu.text: My father kept saying my name when the register stopped recognizing our household. I am grateful for that. I would also like to introduce myself without becoming proof of what happened to us. I am Wei Xiu. I pilot this landing, cut lettering when work is scarce, and dislike ginger tea. The boat I need you to see belongs to none of those facts.

river_chart.speaker: narrator
river_chart.text: She unfolded a chart beneath the shelter. Blue lines marked depth; brown dots marked stones her sounding pole had found. A narrow loop crossed the map twelve times. Beside it lay twelve dates in Wei Xiu's own hand. The route began upstream at an abandoned mooring and returned there every afternoon. Ordinary boats passed outside the loop. No one was trapped aboard the old ferry.

river_limits.speaker: wei_xiu
river_limits.text: It is not eating travelers. I checked before asking anyone to come. The old ferry has no living passengers, no crew, and no cargo we can sell. Its ward pushes other hulls away gently. But the spring current is widening its circuit toward a fishing channel. I can move our route for a week. After that, my promises begin to spend someone else's wages.

river_moran.speaker: mo_ran
river_moran.text: Mine may already have spent more than that. I recognized the stern when Wei Xiu sent the sketch. I crossed on that ferry eleven years ago, after Azure Cloud sentenced me. My ban was from the mountain, not this river. Whatever has changed above us, I still owe an account of what I asked the water to keep.

river_notforgetting.speaker: lin_yue
river_notforgetting.text: You remember the star. You remembered the seal well enough to find us. If the boat took your memories, how could you have carried that knowledge into Azure Cloud? Before we call this another prison, I need to know whether anything was taken from you, or whether the boat is keeping something you chose to leave.

river_echo_rule.speaker: mo_ran
river_echo_rule.text: An echo, not an absence. The ferry keeper offered to preserve the sound of one memory outside my mind. I kept everything I knew. I thought a witness beyond the sect might matter someday. I entrusted the night I first heard the star, including the part where I walked away. Then I waited eleven years to admit why that last part frightened me.

river_sulan.speaker: su_lan
river_sulan.text: Then the boat cannot return a person to a time before their grief. Good. I have heard enough promises of that kind to distrust the price. Can it reveal an echo to anyone who asks? If so, your fear has been floating here as public cargo while you imagined it safely put aside.

river_permission.speaker: mo_ran
river_permission.text: The keeper said an echo could be heard only with its owner's permission. I believed her. Wei Xiu's sketch shows bronze rings around a shadow beneath the ferry. That must be the spirit she served. I have brought the receipt she gave me. An Ru can check the seal; I cannot make an old confidence into present proof by remembering it fondly.

river_receipt.speaker: narrator
river_receipt.text: The receipt had softened along its folds. It named Mo Ran, one entrusted echo, and the east stair of Willow Reach as the agreed place of return. Beneath the seal, a condition read: hold until the owner may receive it safely. The next line set no date and defined no other landing. Lin Yue had seen smaller omissions grow teeth.

river_flood.speaker: wei_xiu
river_flood.text: Willow Reach lost its east stair in last winter's flood. The families moved to high ground; the name on the chart stayed where the stair had been. I asked the old ferry to stop here. It circled past. I asked the shadow why. It rang a bronze ring against the hull. Perhaps that was an answer I did not know how to hear.

river_plan.speaker: lin_yue
river_plan.text: We will stay in your ordinary boat outside its circuit. Mo Ran can identify his own receipt; nobody will open other people's echoes. We will test whether it answers a request before we touch the ward. If the circuit moves toward the fishing channel, tell me at once. A conversation is not useful if the people depending on us cannot wait for it.

river_approach_choice.speaker: wei_xiu
river_approach_choice.text: My sounding pole will keep us clear of the old mooring rope. You can ask Mo Ran to call first, trace the current with me, or listen from outside the circuit until it answers. Each gives us a different kind of knowledge. Choose the one you will trust enough to question when the river disagrees.

choices.text: Let Mo Ran identify himself and offer his receipt.
Survey the circuit with Wei Xiu before speaking.
Listen at the boundary without crossing it.

river_call.speaker: mo_ran
river_call.text: I am the person named on this receipt. I have come to discuss where the echo may be returned. I have not come to hear anyone else's memory. If you remember the keeper who took my seal, tell me how she asked you to carry it. I owe her the courtesy of learning what she actually promised.

river_call_answer.speaker: narrator
river_call_answer.text: The bronze rings beneath the ferry turned toward their boat. A shape rose between them, narrow-headed and long enough to curl twice around the stern. No voice played from the receipt. Mo Ran held it flat until rain threatened the ink; then Wei Xiu put a bowl over his hands. The spirit watched that small shelter before approaching.

river_survey.speaker: wei_xiu
river_survey.text: The circuit follows the old line of the east stair, even where that line crosses deep water now. It bends away from the fishing nets. The ward is making an effort to avoid us, Yue. Something can be careful and still become dangerous. I would like to know what it is trying to protect before we decide which rope to cut.

river_survey_answer.speaker: narrator
river_survey_answer.text: Wei Xiu laid three floating reeds across the current and timed their passage. The ferry slowed before every net marker, then hastened toward the vanished stair. Beneath its hull, bronze rings turned against the flow. A long slate body rose into view. Lin Yue saw the strain in its fins and lowered the sword she had not meant to draw.

river_listen.speaker: lin_yue
river_listen.text: One ring sounds when the boat reaches the vanished stair. Another answers when it turns away. There is room between them for a word. I will say nothing into that room until I know it is waiting for us. Let the next circuit finish. If it turns toward the nets, we move first and interpret later.

river_listen_answer.speaker: narrator
river_listen_answer.text: They waited through a circuit. The first ring sounded over empty water; the second trembled without striking the hull. Between them came a breath like rain caught in a gutter. Lin Yue asked whether the keeper could hear her. A narrow head surfaced beyond the ward, and an amber eye regarded the ordinary boat without crossing its side.

river_spirit.speaker: mooring_eel
river_spirit.text: I hear the name on that paper. I hear the people beside it. The keeper told me to hold the echoes until their owners returned safely to the stair. The stair is water now. When I reach it, there is no place to set a passenger down. I turn away. When I turn away, the promise tells me I have not arrived.

river_boundaries.speaker: su_lan
river_boundaries.text: You have no living passengers aboard. The pilot has checked. Does the promise require a body to step onto the stair, or an echo to reach its owner? I am not asking you to guess. Tell us the words you were given, and tell us where your own understanding begins.

river_keeper_words.speaker: mooring_eel
river_keeper_words.text: One echo, one owner, one safe return. The keeper used the stair because everyone knew it. The rings keep the permission given for each echo; they do not let me search a mind or choose a new owner. Her last instructions were written when the stair still existed. I have been obeying a place after the people left it.

river_keeper_fate.speaker: wei_xiu
river_keeper_fate.text: The keeper died two summers ago. Her niece brought me the landing keys and the old ferry remained tied to its own ward. That is why nobody changed the agreement after the flood. I should have checked what work was still being done under those keys. You are not the only one here who inherited a duty without reading all of it.

river_notfree.speaker: mooring_eel
river_notfree.text: If I break the return line alone, the rings will spill their echoes into the current. They are not minds, but they are confidences. Fish will not care whose sorrow they hear. People will. I can hold the boat here while you speak, if your pilot marks a safe margin. I cannot hold it against spring water forever.

river_margin.speaker: narrator
river_margin.text: Wei Xiu placed a reed marker where the ordinary boat could turn without striking a net. The Eel shortened its circuit to that marker. Its fins whitened under the new pressure. Su Lan untied the clapper from her wrist but did not offer it. Mo Ran lowered his receipt. For a moment, the only sound was rain, which asked nothing of them.

river_first_offer.speaker: lin_yue
river_first_offer.text: We can change the return place with your agreement and Mo Ran's. We can repair a receiving platform above the old stair if it remains safe. We can also pause the ferry in a sheltered reach while the owners decide what should happen to their echoes. None of those permits us to listen. Which can you bear to discuss first?

river_resolution_choice.speaker: mo_ran
river_resolution_choice.text: I will make one decision now: the echo remains sealed while we work. What I entrusted is an account of my hesitation, not a key that should be turned in every lock. Help me ask for a safe return, or help me make a place where it can keep waiting without consuming its keeper.

choices.text: Negotiate a new return place with the owner and spirit.
Survey a replacement stair with the pilot.
Arrange a temporary harbor while every owner is contacted.

river_return_terms.speaker: mo_ran
river_return_terms.text: I authorize return to the north landing, provided the pilot finds a berth safe for both boats and the Eel accepts the revised line. That permission is mine alone. An Ru may witness the document; she may not hear the echo through it. I would rather carry my own unfinished account than leave the spirit carrying an instruction nobody can fulfill.

ending_river_return.speaker: narrator
ending_river_return.text: Mo Ran carried a sealed case from the north landing. Luo Fen's ring waited for her named berth; the third remained closed while the records were searched. The Eel no longer circled the vanished stair. Before leaving, Lin Yue checked the mooring pin Wei Xiu had replaced. One crossing had ended. The remaining promises had a place to rest and people responsible for asking about them.

river_stair_terms.speaker: wei_xiu
river_stair_terms.text: We will sound the bank before anyone brings timber. A rebuilt stair that disappears in the next flood merely gives the promise another season to fail. If the old name can identify a safe landing above the water, the owners can approve it. If it cannot, I will say so even after we have carried all the beams here.

ending_river_stair.speaker: narrator
ending_river_stair.text: The ramp opened above the flood line, with another berth named for high water. Mo Ran and Luo Fen carried their sealed echoes away. The third ring waited at the sheltered mooring under an agreement that could be reviewed without opening it. Wei Xiu left the vanished stair on the chart. A new shore had become safe without pretending the old one had never existed.

river_harbor_terms.speaker: su_lan
river_harbor_terms.text: Then I will lend the clapper as a signal, not an order. One soft stroke means the harbor crew is ready; silence means wait. The spirit may stop before it reaches exhaustion. We will ask the owners where their echoes should go, and we will pay the crew for the time we are asking them to give.

ending_river_harbor.speaker: narrator
ending_river_harbor.text: At the sheltered reach, the old ferry stopped circling. Mo Ran received his sealed echo. Luo Fen chose to ask another question before naming a return day, and the last ring waited while copies were searched. The clapper sounded when a watch was ready. The harbor had not ended every obligation. It had made a place where an unanswered question no longer required a body to exhaust itself.

return_berth.speaker: narrator
return_berth.text: Wei Xiu brought the ordinary boat alongside the landing without inviting the old ferry after it. She tested two mooring posts; one moved under her hand. Lin Yue had been preparing the words of a new covenant. Now she held a hammer while the pilot replaced a rotten pin. The Eel rested at the funded sheltered mooring. Nobody asked it to hold the old ferry against the current while they repaired this different berth.

return_cost.speaker: wei_xiu
return_cost.text: The berth is sound now. It was sound because we checked it, not because someone wrote that it ought to be. Your new return line needs a person who can refuse a landing when conditions change. I can do that this month. In summer I work upriver. Put the next pilot's duty beside mine, or this paper will become another vanished stair.

return_unknown.speaker: lin_yue
return_unknown.text: Then we can make a rule for the third ring without inventing an owner. No one hears it. No one claims it because nobody answers a letter. We record the broken chain of custody and ask the upstream landing to search its copies. Does that give you a promise you can keep, Eel, or does it move the impossible stair into a book?

return_limit.speaker: mooring_eel
return_limit.text: I can keep a closed ring in sheltered water without carrying the ferry around it. The circuit costs me more than the echo does. But I cannot name a stranger by looking at a sound I have no permission to hear. Give me a place where closed things may remain closed, and someone who will ask the question again when you leave.

return_custodian.speaker: su_lan
return_custodian.text: I will be the first contact at this landing. An Ru will keep the record; neither of us can replace the owner. If I leave or die, the work must pass through an explicit acceptance, not through my house keys. I learned that from the bell. A person can refuse a duty they inherit without abandoning the people who depend on it.

return_safety_choice.speaker: mo_ran
return_safety_choice.text: For my own ring, I can accept the echo today or request that it remain sealed here until I am ready. I will not use unreadiness to make the keeper wait without support. I have money for a watch and hands for a mooring rope. Yue, help me choose how to take responsibility without making courage into a performance.

choices.text: Return the sealed case now; Mo Ran decides when to open it.
Reserve a supported watch and a date to reconsider.

return_now.speaker: lin_yue
return_now.text: Receiving it is not the same as displaying it. Let the ring close around a reed case. Mo Ran will carry the case; everyone else will sign only that we saw the return happen. The contents remain his. If he asks us to hear them later, that will be another decision, made with people who can still say no.

return_now_cost.speaker: narrator
return_now_cost.text: An Ru found a clean reed case in her satchel. Mo Ran held it between both hands while the Eel touched its rim with a bronze ring. No voice escaped. The case grew heavier by less than a mouthful of water. Lin Yue signed the return line and noticed how little ink it took to make a boundary that people had spent eleven years avoiding.

return_later.speaker: mo_ran
return_later.text: Eight days from today, then we ask again. Credit the already paid interim turns before calculating my additional watch payment; the clerk will record its start, end and net cost. I will cover only that new coverage, with unused money returned. If the keeper cannot bear another day, the case can come to me sealed before the date. Waiting is a request, not an order to the river. Put that beside my name.

return_later_cost.speaker: narrator
return_later_cost.text: They arranged the watch before accepting payment. Two crew members volunteered; a third declined because her father needed care. Wei Xiu wrote a replacement turn herself. The Eel brought the ring to the sheltered side of the marker and rested. On the eighth day, Mo Ran received the sealed case. Nobody applauded. A crew member handed him a bowl of rice that had gone cold.

return_common.speaker: an_ru
return_common.text: The other two rings remain under separate agreements. Luo Fen may authorize a place of return in her reply. The unidentified ring stays sealed while the copies are searched. Today's document changes no owner's permission except Mo Ran's. I have written that four times because readers tend to mistake an example for a rule that already includes them.

return_moran.speaker: mo_ran
return_moran.text: I used to think preserving this echo was proof that I had been right about the star. It also preserved a night when I heard suffering and went home. Both are true. I may ask you to listen someday, Yue. Today I would rather learn what to do with the part of my life that cannot be settled by proving someone else wrong.

return_yue.speaker: lin_yue
return_yue.text: Then we can mend the boat before you decide. I came here expecting another seal to break. Instead, you handed me a hammer. The star's freedom did not make us experts in every kind of waiting. I am beginning to think a promise needs more than a beautiful last sentence. It needs somebody who knows which mooring post is rotten.

return_letter.speaker: narrator
return_letter.text: Luo Fen's reply arrived in the hand of a fish seller: she wanted her echo returned at the high-bank landing and did not permit anyone else to hear it. An Ru entered the request. The missing page would take longer to find. The Eel slept between watches, its bronze rings resting against wood rather than turning endlessly beneath a ferry.

river_book.speaker: an_ru
river_book.text: Su Lan sent a shore runner for me. Mo Ran's receipt matches the landing book. It records three echoes: his, Luo Fen's, and one whose custody page was lost before I received it. Luo Fen is alive, a carpenter at Willow Reach. The third ring's outside reference is illegible; its enclosed receipt stays sealed. A claimant may offer a counterfoil, but matching it requires a readable exterior custody record. We will search the missing page, not open the private copy to manufacture an owner.

stair_soundings.speaker: narrator
stair_soundings.text: Wei Xiu took them upstream in her ordinary boat while the Eel rested at the funded sheltered mooring. Its stopped ferry did not resume the exhausted circuit merely because they chose to build a ramp. Willow Reach had moved without changing its name. New roofs stood above the broken bank. At the vanished east stair, a lintel lay underwater. A woman on the high bank asked whether they had come to measure timber. The survey would examine that landing without spending the spirit's body.

stair_luofen.speaker: wei_xiu
stair_luofen.text: That is Luo Fen. Her letter reached my father this morning; she received our first message before we left. She wants her echo returned, but not heard by the work crew. She has offered to inspect the new platform herself. The flood took her stair, not her skill. Ask her about the joints before asking me.

stair_measure.speaker: narrator
stair_measure.text: Luo Fen marked a beam with a carpenter's square, then showed Wei Xiu the old flood line. The new bank looked firm until a sounding pole slipped through its crust. Beneath it lay a pocket of water. The carpenter shook her head. Her household had already rebuilt once. She would not give her name to a stair that borrowed stability from the next dry week.

stair_alternative.speaker: lin_yue
stair_alternative.text: Then we should abandon this patch before the beams make us stubborn. The stone shelf above it looks sound, but a person with a weak knee could not climb there alone. A safe landing must include getting home after the boat stops. Wei Xiu, can the shelf take a ramp without pushing the current toward the fishing nets?

stair_tradeoff.speaker: wei_xiu
stair_tradeoff.text: A narrow ramp can. A grand stair cannot. We will need two turns, a resting rail, and a removable lower section for high water. It will cost more rope and less carved stone. Luo Fen says she can supervise the joints. She has not offered to work for free. I am glad she said that before anyone called her contribution a gift.

stair_money.speaker: su_lan
stair_money.text: The shrine has maintenance money held through winter. Its terms cover ferry access for visitors. They do not cover every repair we can describe as kind. I will ask the household meeting to authorize the part serving that access. Mo Ran can pay for the separate receiving case. The rest must be named before a worker picks up a saw.

stair_funding_choice.speaker: wei_xiu
stair_funding_choice.text: The shrine meeting approved the ferry-access share; the clerk separated it from Mo Ran's receiving-case payment. The remaining ramp work needs its own funding. We can build in paid local stages using money actually released, or ask the upriver boat association for an advance against agreed maintenance work. The first takes longer; the second binds a season of wages. No stage begins on an anticipated grant. Choose the cost to put before the people who will bear it.

choices.text: Build in paid stages, keeping an interim berth open.
Negotiate the advance with a fixed repayment ceiling.

stair_stages.speaker: lin_yue
stair_stages.text: Keep the temporary berth outside the spirit's circuit. Put its limits beside the pilot's rota, not at the bottom of the work notice. We will pay each shift before inviting the next. If funds run short, we stop at a safe stage. A slow ramp is a delay people can plan for; an unfinished dangerous one is another promise that spends their bodies.

stair_stages_cost.speaker: narrator
stair_stages_cost.text: The first stage took six days. Lin Yue carried boards; Mo Ran sorted pegs; Luo Fen sent a crooked joint back three times. Wei Xiu kept the ordinary boats running from the temporary berth. At sunset she paid the workers in a line that moved more slowly than any sword lesson. Nobody described the extra days as failure. They described whose turn came tomorrow.

stair_advance.speaker: an_ru
stair_advance.text: Then the ceiling includes missed work during high water. No household's land secures the debt. The association may collect only the maintenance turns named in the agreement, and every turn must have a replacement option. I will read those conditions before the amount. If the lender refuses them, the attractive number on the next line will not decide for us.

stair_advance_cost.speaker: narrator
stair_advance_cost.text: The association accepted a smaller advance with a longer schedule. Wei Xiu crossed out the first amount rather than tearing up its record. Luo Fen kept a copy beside her tools. The advance bought the first timber delivery before the shifts began; the first construction stage took six days. Pilots would spend part of summer tending posts instead of carrying goods. When Lin Yue praised the bargain, Wei Xiu showed her the hours that praise had left out.

stair_charter.speaker: an_ru
stair_charter.text: The receiving place is Willow Reach's high-bank platform, with the north landing named for high water. Each owner must authorize their own return. Mo Ran has signed. Luo Fen has signed without consenting to a public hearing of her echo. The third ring stays sealed at the sheltered mooring while we search for its receipt. A safe platform does not supply a missing permission.

stair_test.speaker: narrator
stair_test.text: Before the old ferry approached, Wei Xiu tested an ordinary boat with secured sand ballast equal to its rated load and no passengers. She turned it along the surveyed route while two crew members watched from shore. Luo Fen carried two sand sacks over the ramp; the carpenter checked deflection and fasteners separately. Su Lan tested the rail. Lin Yue kept her field closed. Unfueled joints had to carry the design load after every visitor left. A successful turn did not replace the carpenter's signed structural check.

stair_spirit.speaker: mooring_eel
stair_spirit.text: I can reach that wood without turning toward the vanished stair. The rings whose owners accepted it may come ashore. The closed ring may wait beside the marker with me. The new line asks a pilot to judge the river before I approach. I can accept a promise that lets the pilot stop me. I could not have carved that permission for myself.

stair_return.speaker: narrator
stair_return.text: Mo Ran received a sealed reed case. Luo Fen received another and took it straight to her house, refusing every curious invitation along the way. The Eel moved its last closed ring to the sheltered mooring. Above the old stair, Wei Xiu cut the survey date into stone. She left the previous flood mark visible below it, where another spring could contradict today's careful measurements.

stair_after.speaker: mo_ran
stair_after.text: When I crossed eleven years ago, I wanted a witness that no disciple could silence. I did not ask what work that witness would need to keep doing. This ramp will require people who may never hear what I left. I am paying my part because their work exists whether I am ready to tell a noble story about my own.

harbor_site.speaker: narrator
harbor_site.text: The sheltered reach lay behind a willow bank, close enough to the north landing for a crew to walk home. Wei Xiu sounded it twice, once in the ordinary boat and once from the bank. The Eel waited outside while a fishing family moved a net they had set there. Lin Yue offered payment. The family accepted it without being asked to call the interruption a public service.

harbor_rules.speaker: wei_xiu
harbor_rules.text: No one ties a ring to a mooring post. The spirit keeps the echoes, and the boat rests beside it. The crew watches the river and calls for a move if the current turns. We are providing a place to wait, not acquiring a cargo. Put the fishing channel on the chart before the shelter. It was somebody's work before it became our solution.

harbor_spirit.speaker: mooring_eel
harbor_spirit.text: Here I can hold the return line without following the old circuit. The keeper allowed a stop wherever the ferry could wait safely; I mistook waiting for something only passengers could need. If the harbor becomes unsafe, I will move to the marker you name. I will not open a ring to pay for my place here.

harbor_sulan.speaker: su_lan
harbor_sulan.text: Nor will anyone demand that you do. The clapper belongs to me and remains on loan. I will lend it to one watch at a time, then ask whether the next crew accepts the task. A sound made without a willing watch will mean nothing. That is a small enough command for me to trust myself with.

harbor_budget.speaker: narrator
harbor_budget.text: An Ru drew two columns. In one she put the net payment, lamp oil, mooring repair, and replacement watch wages, crediting Wei Xiu's interim reserve. In the other she put the money already offered. The gap was larger than Lin Yue's purse. Mo Ran laid down his remaining travel silver. It closed less than half. Their proposal now had a shape a refusal could touch.

harbor_shortage.speaker: mo_ran
harbor_shortage.text: I can work, but I cannot promise that my hands replace a trained pilot. I can also give the money I set aside for going somewhere no one knows me. I had imagined that journey as freedom. Spending part of it here may be freedom too. Spending it all would leave me dependent on people who might prefer my gratitude to my answer.

harbor_watch_choice.speaker: lin_yue
harbor_watch_choice.text: We can fund a small paid watch for eight days and ask again with the replies in hand. Or we can ask the boat association to maintain the berth as part of its regular work, with the spirit's refusal written into the charter. Either requires less than promising every future hour. Which agreement should we offer first?

choices.text: Fund eight days, with a reserve for moving to safety.
Offer a regular berth agreement the spirit may leave.

harbor_eight_days.speaker: an_ru
harbor_eight_days.text: Then the reserve cannot be used to make the watches look generous. It pays for an emergency move even if no owner answers. The eighth day is a meeting date, not an eviction. If the money runs short, we ask for a smaller watch or another berth before anyone learns the limit by finding the lanterns dark.

harbor_eight_cost.speaker: narrator
harbor_eight_cost.text: Lin Yue sold the silver clasp from her travel bundle. It bought oil and one more night, not a permanent answer. Mo Ran kept enough money to leave if he chose. Su Lan declined to praise them as selfless. Instead she wrote their names beside the amounts, so the next meeting would know whose offer could be renewed and whose could not.

harbor_association.speaker: wei_xiu
harbor_association.text: The association can include the berth in its morning inspection if the spirit agrees. It cannot promise a keeper at every hour. We will publish those limits and name a place to call for help. I will ask the crews privately before the charter is read. I know how easily a public invitation turns the first yes into pressure on everyone behind it.

harbor_association_cost.speaker: narrator
harbor_association_cost.text: Four crews accepted inspection turns. Two offered only money, and one asked to be left out because its hull needed repair. The charter recorded all seven answers without assigning virtue. The Eel accepted the berth after hearing its limits. When the first inspection boat arrived, the spirit moved aside without being signaled. They had given each other a habit that did not require obedience.

harbor_letters.speaker: an_ru
harbor_letters.text: The letters name no contents. Luo Fen receives her receipt number and an invitation to choose a return place.
